slash_art.teblade.judgement_cut_dread_st: An enhanced Judgement Cut. Tap during the art to follow with a thrust, or hold to add forward movement.
slash_art.teblade.rainshower.desc: Calls down a Heavy Rain phantom sword array upon the locked-on target.
slash_art.teblade.earth_art.desc: Attempts to teleport to a locked-on target if one is present, then strikes nearby enemies with a shock that knocks them back and slows them; a perfect cast also reduces armor and briefly roots non-player targets.
slash_art.teblade.flame_art.desc: Attempts to teleport to a locked-on target if one is present, then delivers two fiery slashes ahead that ignite enemies on hit; a perfect cast adds three area bursts ahead without damaging blocks.
slash_art.teblade.growth_art.desc: Attempts to teleport to a locked-on target if one is present, then slashes nearby enemies and restores health; a perfect cast restores more health and briefly grants Resistance.
slash_art.teblade.sky_art.desc: Attempts to teleport to a locked-on target if one is present, then unleashes a piercing slash ahead, calculating damage against half the target's armor; a perfect cast increases damage and reach.
slash_art.teblade.thunder_art.desc: Attempts to teleport to a locked-on target if one is present, then dashes forward three times, slashing enemies along the path and launching them with the final hit; a perfect cast adds two lightning slashes that briefly stun targets, or slow players.
slash_art.teblade.tide_art.desc: Attempts to teleport to a locked-on target if one is present, then dashes forward twice, slashing enemies along the path and slowing them by 40% for 3 seconds; a perfect cast also roots targets for 1 second and applies vanilla freezing that naturally decays over about 2 seconds. Burning clears freezing; players are only slowed. Dashes cannot pass through blocks.
se.teblade.automatic.desc: Automatically releases SA at the right moment while the use key is held.
se.teblade.fox_wish_snow_wish.desc: Damage carries additional powder snow damage. Powder snow damage taken instead restores health.
se.teblade.hour_of_judgment.desc: Removes the three-cast limit on perfect SA.
se.teblade.sudden_rain.desc: While unbroken, taking durability damage summons a special raining phantom sword formation above the locked-on target.
se.teblade.witness_rainbow.desc: While broken, durability damage instead repairs the blade, and slashes become stronger special slashes.
se.teblade.bloodthirst.desc: Direct melee hits restore health proportional to actual damage dealt; the restoration ratio increases when your health is low. Restores at most 2 health per hit and 2 per second.
se.teblade.earth.desc: Reduces damage taken and knockback strength while held in the main hand.
se.teblade.flame.desc: Melee attacks ignite targets and deal increased damage to burning targets.
se.teblade.flux_blade.desc: Attacks deal additional flux pollution damage.
se.teblade.growth.desc: Slowly restores durability while the blade is not broken.
se.teblade.mystery_rite.desc: Each perfect SA cast grants 1 stack, up to 3; at 3 stacks, the next successful SA cast consumes all three to waive its proud soul cost, then grants this cast's perfect reward. Failed casts do not change stacks.
se.teblade.sky.desc: Briefly increases movement speed and SlashBlade damage after a perfect SA cast; ends when switching weapons.
se.teblade.taint_mark.desc: Attacks apply Corrosion to the target, reducing armor by 2 per stack, up to 5 stacks for 8 seconds. Applying or refreshing it adds 1 temporary warp to yourself.
se.teblade.thunder.desc: Increases movement speed while held in the main hand; attacks while sprinting deal additional unattributed lightning damage proportional to the hit.
se.teblade.tide.desc: Direct melee hits build stacks on the target (cleared if not hit again within 3 seconds). Reaching 3 stacks clears them and briefly slows the target, taking the stronger effect between this and Slowness without stacking.
se.teblade.vis_repair.desc: Continuously consumes Vis from a carried wand to repair the blade.
se.teblade.void_step.desc: Grants brief invulnerability after an SA hits a target, with an 8-second cooldown.
effect.teblade.earth_root.desc: Prevents voluntary walking without locking the view or blocking movement caused by external forces.
effect.teblade.tide_slow.desc: Reduces movement speed by 20% per level; takes the stronger effect between this and Slowness without stacking.

research.teblade.blade_revert.title: Reversion
research.teblade.blade_revert.stage_0:
Infusion pours aspects into a blade, yet a blade should not be locked into a single purpose forever. The original Rodai foundation is still there, and what was added later ought to be distinguishable.
I want to try separating the two layers with §5Salis Mundus§r. Stripping away an infused effect, of course, is nothing like getting back the crystals and essentia spent to make it.
research.teblade.blade_revert.stage_1:
Sprinkling Salis Mundus along the boundary left by infusion withdraws the Six Breaths and returns the blade to its family's Rodai form. §5Reversion§r preserves the blade's original foundation and growth, while everything added with the elemental form is removed.
That way, when I wish to take another path later, I only give up this infusion rather than throwing away all the effort spent raising the blade.
research.teblade.blade_rodai.title: The Name of Rodai
research.teblade.blade_rodai.stage_0:
Making greatwood and silverwood wand cores showed me how well wood can carry magic.
I plan to follow that line of thought and start by crafting sheathed wooden blade blanks.§5"Greatwood Dummy"§r and §5"Silverwood Shirasaya"§r serve as two fitting starting points. As for what each is suited to bear, I will have to test them material by material rather than judging from wand cores alone.
research.teblade.blade_rodai.stage_1:
The wooden blade blanks give me a form I can rework, though what nature to leave on the edge is still unsettled.
Fortunately, history records blades known as §5"Rodai"§r. With them as a reference, I can bring my past experience in alchemy and infusion into bladesmithing much faster.
research.teblade.breath_earth.title: Six Breaths: Earth
research.teblade.breath_earth.stage_0:
Whether digging or placing blocks across an area, the Shovel of the Earthmover always spreads its force along a fixed orientation. Digging dirt is useless for a blade, of course, but that way of spreading force across the ground is well worth borrowing.
I need to reexamine how a §5Terra Crystal§r connects to the earth and crafting aspects. If force is spread beneath an enemy's feet, can it shake their footing just as it shifts soil and stone?
research.teblade.breath_earth.stage_1:
My calculations were right. Spreading force outward from the wielder lets §5Earth§r push enemies back with a tremor and slow them. On a perfect cast, it also briefly roots targets and weakens their armor, opening a gap for the next strike.
While held in the main hand, §5Stalwart Earth§r also lessens the damage and knockback you take. Push the enemy away, and your own stance grows all the steadier.
research.teblade.breath_flame.title: Six Breaths: Flame
research.teblade.breath_flame.stage_0:
The Pickaxe of the Core can sense ores because the fire within it works not through heat alone, but by being guided toward metal and the senses. Bladesmithing has no need for prospecting, yet this way of guiding fire is what I am looking for.
First I should compare a §5Ignis Crystal§r against the fire and metal aspects again. If flame can cling to the edge, the momentum left by successive slashes might not end when the blade is sheathed.
research.teblade.breath_flame.stage_1:
§5Flame§r leaves fire behind through two successive slashes, keeping enemies burning even after the edge has passed. On a perfect cast, it also fixes a point ahead of the opening stance where three bursts detonate in succession.
The edge itself also takes on the §5Blazing Heart§r trait: ordinary melee attacks ignite the target, and striking an already burning enemy deals heavier damage.
research.teblade.breath_growth.title: Six Breaths: Growth
research.teblade.breath_growth.stage_0:
The Hoe of Growth uses the power of order to spur plants on, even affecting species untouched by ordinary bone meal. Still, growth is never a simple repetition of what came before; branches and leaves always bring forth new changes.
I plan to compare an §5Ordo Crystal§r and a §5Perditio Crystal§r side by side. With the plant aspect's help, perhaps guidance and change can coexist and point to a use suited for a blade.
research.teblade.breath_growth.stage_1:
Once the power of growth spreads outward with a slash, it can also flow back to the wielder to mend wounds. §5Growth§r does not need to draw life from an enemy; simply executing the art restores health, while a perfect cast heals more and leaves brief protection against harm.
Meanwhile, the growth remaining within the blade itself becomes §5Growth§r, slowly repairing the edge on its own.
research.teblade.breath_sky.title: Six Breaths: Sky
research.teblade.breath_sky.stage_0:
The Spear of the Sky pours the momentum built up during a sprint into its target, hurling it high into the air. Air excels at carrying momentum, yet must the wielder really run the whole distance in person?
I want to use an §5Aer Crystal§r to rethink the link between movement and energy. If momentum can break free directly from the edge, the slash should reach afar even while the wielder stays in place.
research.teblade.breath_sky.stage_1:
If the wielder does not charge forward with the wind, the momentum must be gathered before the edge and sent out along a straight line at once. That is the way of §5Sky§r. On a perfect cast, it pierces farther and hits harder, cutting the target's armor value in half as it passes through.
Any momentum not spent on that slash lingers briefly as §5Swift Sky§r, quickening your steps and strengthening the primary slashes that follow.
research.teblade.breath_thunder.title: Six Breaths: Thunder
research.teblade.breath_thunder.stage_0:
The Sword of the Zephyr can both call forth leaping arcs of lightning and raise a whirlwind to push nearby objects away. If wind can drive external things forward, a wielder should be able to ride that same gale into a dash.
I need to look again at how an §5Aer Crystal§r pairs with the movement and conflict aspects. So long as the wind carries the slash forward, the blade need not stand still and borrow the wind from afar.
research.teblade.breath_thunder.stage_1:
By dashing with the wind, slashes sweep across every enemy along the path. §5Thunder§r chains three forward dashes and finishes with a rising slash; on a perfect cast, it adds two lightning slashes at the end. Wind closes the distance, and lightning leaves the enemy no time to strike back.
Even while simply holding the blade, §5Swift Thunder§r quickens your pace. Land a direct hit while sprinting, and lingering lightning cleaves out with the edge—no need to wait for a sword art to call upon wind and thunder.
research.teblade.breath_tide.title: Six Breaths: Tide
research.teblade.breath_tide.stage_0:
The Axe of the Stream fells connected timber starting from the farthest block, yet the fallen logs flow right back to hand with the current. Pairing water with plants clearly lets force run to places normally out of reach.
I want to start from an §5Aqua Crystal§r and see whether that flowing force can carry the wielder toward the enemy, then drag at their steps after the clash.
research.teblade.breath_tide.stage_1:
§5Tide§r rides the current into two successive forward dashes, weighting the slashes along the way with slowness. On a perfect cast, it first roots the target and then freezes it right after. Rather than chasing a heavier blow, keeping the enemy from pulling away at all is clearly the better bargain.
Ordinary direct hits leave a layer of §5Tide§r moisture; at three stacks it disperses and slows the target.
research.teblade.primordial_curse.title: Primordial Curse
research.teblade.primordial_curse.requir: You must first complete the infusion of §5Demon Sword "Primordial" Curse§r at an infusion altar.
research.teblade.primordial_curse.stage_:
Research into the §5Primordial Pearl§r still has no settled answer: either it is a remnant left from the dawn of creation, or it comes from a place that does not obey known magical laws.
Both claims remain conjecture, yet the pure primal aspects inside it behave in a most unusual way.One thing is certain: its potential far exceeds ordinary materials, perhaps enough to withstand a more extreme infusion-forging.
I plan to place an elemental blade at the center, set four Rodai blades and the remaining offerings around it, and force them together into one.

I have named this design §5Demon Sword "Primordial" Curse§r.
So long as my calculations hold, it will become an edge no thaumaturge in the world has ever conceived.
The altar is ready. It is time to witness the birth of this masterpiece.

My hands are still trembling as I write this down. The eerie presence radiating from the blade still lingers over the infusion altar—only when I gripped its hilt did I realize what I had actually made.It is powerful, without question: powerful enough to draw upon warp directly to rend enemies apart, powerful enough to turn the very flux in the air into its cutting edge, powerful enough that... the moment I drew it from its sheath, the first thought to cross my mind was to turn the point upon myself.I once heard of a bladesmith who was wounded by a weapon of his own making, and sealed his forge never to smith again.
Perhaps this is the price of forging such a weapon—the price of defying the heavens.
research.teblade.rodai_blood.title: What Crimson Leaves Behind
research.teblade.rodai_blood.stage_0:
More than half the characters in §5Crimson Rites§r are unreadable, and what the eye-opening ritual might call forth remains unclear. Yet the few passages I can barely make out all bind power together with life.
A §5Crimson Blade§r can give you a more concrete reference: the book's words cannot all be trusted, but so long as part of that power remains in the metal, there is a place to begin.
research.teblade.rodai_blood.stage_1:
There is no need to decipher the whole ritual; the clues left on the Crimson Blade are enough. Reforged with "Silverwood Shirasaya", the blade not only repairs itself, but its edge also links the enemy's life to yours—this is §5Bloodthirst§r.
Wounds dealt directly by the blade restore its wielder; the more gravely hurt you are, the more effective that exchange becomes.
research.teblade.rodai_mystery.title: Thaumium in the Edge
research.teblade.rodai_mystery.stage_0:
Thaumium is sturdier than iron and accepts enchantments more readily. Yet if I want to forge a blade from it, flipping through notes on metallurgy is not enough—I need to see how it performs once made into a weapon.
First I must obtain a §5Thaumium Sword§r for a side-by-side comparison. There is no need to copy the sword's shape; I only care which properties remain after reforging.
research.teblade.rodai_mystery.stage_1:
I used "Silverwood Shirasaya" to receive the thaumium, then completed the reforging with Salis Mundus.
The metal's high affinity for magic gave me an idea: when a sword art is executed properly, the proud souls that would normally scatter can be gathered back in the same motion and kept for the next strike. I call this way of storing them §5Mystery Rite§r.
research.teblade.rodai_taint.title: The Mark of Taint
research.teblade.rodai_taint.stage_0:
Concentrated flux brings forth taint the moment it touches matter. Bottling it up to throw is only one way to use it; there is no need for me to scatter it wide.
I want to compare a §5Vitium Crystal§r with "Silverwood Shirasaya" first. If that contact can be confined to the edge, I can put it to use on a blade without relying on its spread.
research.teblade.rodai_taint.stage_1:
After eroding "Greatwood Dummy" with a Vitium Crystal, any target touched by the edge has its armor steadily eaten away by the §5Corrosion§r upon it.
Yet why did it have to be greatwood? And what... is the price of doing this?
research.teblade.rodai_void.title: A Rift in the Void
research.teblade.rodai_void.stage_0:
While studying void seeds, I noticed that starkly contradictory properties can coexist in the same metal, and damage to it even mends itself. It seems the boundaries of a material are not as rigid as they appear.
I need to find a §5Void Sword§r and examine it. If those properties remain once the metal is fixed into a sword's form, perhaps it can be used to reforge a blade blank.
research.teblade.rodai_void.stage_1:
The metal of a Void Sword mends itself, so using "Silverwood Shirasaya" to receive it makes repairing the blade easy enough. What interests me more is another question: is the metal itself the only thing it can mend?
Field testing proved it: when a sword art strikes an enemy, the blade and its wielder can briefly borrow a layer of shelter from the §5Void§r. Focusing only on the blade body before was far too narrow a view.
research.teblade.scanned.slashblade.titl: The Shape and Soul of a Blade
research.teblade.scanned.slashblade.stag:
By chance, I examined the blade at my side through a Thaumometer.
Behind the lens appeared three aspects I had never seen before: §5Slash Blade§r, §5Evil Spirit§r, and §5Proud Soul§r. §5Slash Blade§r refers to more than a metal edge, encompassing the form of blade and sheath together; §5Evil Spirit§r and §5Proud Soul§r correspond to the souls absorbed by the blade in battle.That made me realize I might be able to work out a way of bladesmithing that belongs to thaumaturges.
I should write this observation down first. It calls for deeper study.
research.teblade.six_breaths.title: Six Breaths
research.teblade.six_breaths.stage_0:
Each of the four Rodai blades takes a different metal and keeps that metal's temper even after reforging.
Yet a blade's strength does not lie in the elements. If the primal breaths are to be blended into the edge as well, I must first sort out what place aspects, traits, and sword arts each hold in a blade—which part can be replaced through infusion, and which must remain in the blade itself.
research.teblade.six_breaths.stage_1:
Water on the Axe of the Stream is used to gather timber, while wind on a weapon is used to blow things away. Both rely on infusion, yet the actual use depends on the implement itself; the tricks of elemental tools cannot be copied onto a blade unchanged.
Even so, the underlying approach of elemental tool infusion is well worth borrowing.I have provisionally named this method §5Six Breaths§r. Rather than forging a new blade from scratch, expanding directly upon an existing Rodai is clearly more worthwhile.A blade's foundation decides what it can endure, while the infused aspects rewrite its techniques. That way, Six Breaths has no need for six new materials: simply infusing the matching aspects replaces the sword art and adds the corresponding trait and finished enchantments, all while keeping the Rodai family's original nature.
Of course, the growth already accumulated on the blade carries over with it, whereas wear and damage cannot be wiped away by infusion—no different from the old ways of bladesmithing.
research.teblade.unlock_bladecraft.title: Discovery: Bladecraft
research.teblade.unlock_bladecraft.stage:
I need to compare a §5Tiny Proud Soul§r alongside those newly discovered aspects.
A blade is no blank vessel. Copying the methods used for elemental tools outright would likely overwrite the blade's original nature.

Experiments proved that while proud souls can be kept outside a blade, a single fragment cannot stand in for the form of a blade, nor can proud soul essentia extracted from it be used to forge one directly.
I have decided to split the research into two steps: first reforge suitable materials into a blade that can withstand infusion, and then reshape what lies within.To keep my notes from getting tangled, I am setting this work apart under its own category: §5Bladecraft§r.
research.teblade.spell_drive.title: Focus Medium: Drive
research.teblade.spell_drive.stage_0:
Even after the blade is sheathed, the slash loosed from its edge keeps hurtling forward. Drive made me realize that spell delivery need not be shaped into a spherical projectile—it can also be formed into a flat, sweeping edge.I can now condense such a blade-shape out of mana, letting it pass through creatures along its path and deliver the focus effects that follow one by one. The same target will only receive a given Drive's delivery once.
However, this §5Drive§r only carries the spell; it deals no slashing damage on its own. Without an effect linked after it, no matter how sharp it looks, it is only an empty shell.
I can raise its range within the focus so the blade-shape flies farther, at the cost of higher complexity.
research.teblade.spell_judgement_cut.sta:
Must a blade cross an enemy's body in person to leave a wound? Judgement Cut gives a very different answer: the slashes can fall directly at a distance, repeatedly slicing open the same small pocket of space.By weaving this structure into a focus, I can leave a cluster of §5Judgement Cut§r at the spell's point of impact, subjecting nearby enemies to successive slashes.
Raising the hit count lets the slashes linger a moment longer, though it also increases the focus's complexity. Rather than trying to make the blade-light fly farther, this time I simply let the edge stop right where it needs to be.
research.teblade.spell_summoned_swords.s:
Summoned swords need neither metal nor hilt; they take form entirely from the wielder's will. Since mana can hold that sword-shape together, I can naturally make it carry a spell as well.The §5Summoned Swords§r medium condenses several flying swords before me and fires them together toward where I aim. They deal no slashing damage by themselves, instead releasing the focus effects they carry upon hit and shatter. Increasing the sword count raises complexity accordingly.Conversely, if the flying swords stop serving as carriers and become the effect itself, the result is §5Summoned Sword Array§r. It deploys a Spiral, Storm, Blistering, or Heavy Rain formation at the spell's target to wound enemies with condensed blades; if there is no suitable creature to anchor to, the array unfolds directly around the impact point.
Both formation and sword count can be tuned in the focus. The medium packs a spell into swords, whereas the array forges the spell directly into swords—similar at a glance, yet meant for completely different uses.
death.attack.teblade.secondary_thunder: %1$s was struck down by lingering lightning

spell.teblade.judgement_cut.desc: Leaves successive slashes at the spell's impact point, cutting nearby enemies.
spell.teblade.summoned_swords.name: Summoned Swords
spell.teblade.summoned_swords.desc: Several phantom swords fired in parallel that release the effects that follow upon hit and shatter. Deals no slashing damage on its own.

spell.teblade.summoned_swords_array.desc: Deploys a phantom sword array at the target: Spiral, Storm, Blistering, or Heavy Rain falling from above.
